name: row_gather
mechanisms: memory.dram.service / memory.l2.service: load-to-use latency of ONE 128-bit global load whose lanes fall on several rows
ownership: gpu-shared (full-GPU loop) for the level latencies; the other lines' clones (fg-line-mem task/fg-mem-share, fg-line-sync) have no commit on memory.l2 / memory.dram latency of plain loads (fg-line-mem works on the async-copy issue gate).
question: How long does a warp wait for one 128-bit global load as a function of the number of distinct rows (lines) its lanes touch, from DRAM and from the L2; and for the block of seven such loads that the flash-MLA sparse gather issues back to back?

why.kernel: flashmla_sparse_decode_v32_h64_03 (H100 full GPU, sim / ncu 0.765; job and journal kept in $A/fg-line-cold/attrib6). Read from the job (MACC / MSEC of the producer warps, $A/fg-line-cold/tools/ldg_lanes.py): every LDG.E.EL.LTC256B.128.CONSTANT of the gather reads 8 token rows (lane l: row l % 8, 16-byte chunk l / 8, so 64 contiguous bytes per row), 20-23 sectors on 8-10 lines; rows are 656 bytes apart in units, not line aligned. It is NOT a lane-contiguous whole-line read (the earlier note said so; corrected here), so the line-granular port rule already applies to it.
why.gap: first block of an iteration (7 loads within 27 cycles: +0x200 with LTC128B, then +0x0 .. +0x140 in steps of 0x40 with LTC256B; the wait is taken at the first use of the second load's data): hardware 1168 cycles per iteration (long scoreboard at that PC, average of 16 iterations), simulation 467 on average (iterations 0-4: 956 / 727 / 664 / 648, falling to 150 by iteration 15 as rows repeat).
why.earlier cells: gather_latency run 1, one warp, one CTA, cold table, 2 scalar loads per lane on 32 lines: 1054-1274 cycles (h100), 1223-1526 (b300), against the single-sector pointer-chase DRAM latency leaf 697.9 (h100) / 874.9 (b300) (memlat). With the table already in the L2 the same cell is 274-514 (leaf 305.5, far hit +159.6): the L2 level agrees, the DRAM level is 350-570 above the leaf.

probe.file: probe/row_gather.cu, 128-bit loads written as inline PTX (ld.global.v4.u32; the hinted form is ld.global.nc.L1::evict_last.L2::256B.v4.u32 / .L2::128B as in the kernel) so that ptxas cannot scalarise them; the SASS gate requires exactly the expected LDG.E...128 forms in the timed window and no other global load there.
probe.single: one load per iteration. Lane l reads 16 bytes of row g = l % L at chunk c = (l / L) % C (C = 1: all lanes of a row read the same 16 bytes; C = 4: 64 contiguous bytes per row, L <= 8). spread = far: row g of an iteration is a random 4-KiB slot of the table (hash of cta, warp, iteration, g), address slot * 4096 + c * 16; spread = adjacent: rows are consecutive 128-byte lines inside one random 4-KiB slot. Lane 0 records clock64 before the load and after the use of the loaded value (x ^ w accumulated into a result that is stored).
probe.block: the kernel's first block: 8 rows per warp (row = lane % 8, chunk = lane / 8), row address = table + index * 656 with a random index per (cta, warp, iteration, row); loads at +0x200 (L2::128B) then +0x0, +0x40, +0x80, +0xc0, +0x100, +0x140 (L2::256B); t_first = clock after the use of the second load's value, t_all = clock after the use of all seven.
probe.passes: in one launch: pass 0 over 32 iterations on a table pushed out of the L2 by reading a 512-MiB buffer before the launch (DRAM); then the warp reads a 4-MiB spoiler buffer (pushes the rows out of its L1, not out of the L2); pass 1 repeats the same rows in the same order (L2).

cells.single (one warp, grid 1): L = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 x hint = plain, kernel, C = 1, far; L = 8, C = 4, far x both hints; L = 32, C = 1, adjacent x both hints
cells.block: W = 1, 4 warps per CTA x grid = 1, all SMs, kernel hints; W = 1, grid 1, plain
cells.table: 1 GiB; 5 launches per cell; iterations 4..31 are read, iteration 0 separately

probe.replay (h100, the engine of main, build-: single far plain L = 1, 8, 32; single L = 8 C = 4 kernel hint; block W = 1 and W = 4, grid 1, kernel hints (one launch each).

derivation: per cell and pass: median, p10, p90 of the wait per iteration (t_first and t_all for block) over iterations 4..31 and launches 1..4.

prediction_from_the_installed_leaves.rule: a request completes at its last sector: level latency + one line of port time per distinct line (128 B / about 122-127 B per cycle), a few cycles of issue and use.
prediction_from_the_installed_leaves.h100: single, pass 0: 715 (L = 1) rising to about 750 (L = 32); pass 1: 320-340 near, 480-500 on the first far hit; no dependence on the hint. block, W = 1: t_first about 730, t_all about 790 (pass 0); 340-560 (pass 1); W = 4 on one SM: t_all up to about 980.
prediction_from_the_installed_leaves.b300: single, pass 0: 890-925; pass 1: 320-340 near (far-hit leaf as installed); block W = 1 pass 0: t_first about 905, t_all about 965.

reading.usable: launches 1..4 agree within 5 % on the medians; SASS gate passed.
reading.R1: every pass-0 cell within 15 % of the prediction: a single gather request is timed correctly; the flash-MLA excess is not in the request latency and the next step is the interaction with the rest of that kernel (role by role in the replay of the kernel itself).
reading.R2: single pass-0 latency grows with L beyond the prediction: the table latency(L, C, spread, hint) is the result; a rule is proposed in an addendum (post hoc) with constants taken from the single cells L <= 16 only and judged on cells they do not come from: L = 32 far, L = 32 adjacent, both block cells with W = 1 (t_first, t_all), and the gather_latency run-1 one-warp cells (1054-1274 h100, 1223-1526 b300); the replay with the rule must be within 15 % of hardware on the block cells.
reading.R3: single cells agree with the prediction but block cells do not: the excess needs several requests outstanding together (ordering of returns inside a warp or an SM); the block table is the result and the next probe varies the number and order of loads.
reading.hint: plain and kernel-hint cells differing by more than 10 % at the same L means the hint changes timing; the converter does not carry it today (MACC cache_hint is 0 on these loads) and that becomes a capture requirement.

not_allowed: no value from full-GPU error; no per-kernel rule.

addenda.usable: pass 1 within 5 % everywhere; about half of the pass-0 cells have launch medians more than 5 % apart (up to 30 %, b300 adjacent). The cause is in the reading below (levels by address plus occasional slow accesses), so the criterion is not met as written and the pass-0 medians are read together with their distributions.

reading (R2; pass 0 = DRAM, one warp, on.32 adjacent lines in one 4-KiB slot: h100 888, b300 1026: less than 32 far rows, so the growth is by separate locations, not by lines.
reading (R2; pass 0 = DRAM, one warp, on.hint: kernel-hint cells are 0 .. 9 % above plain at the same L (one cell 8.8 %, the rest below 5 %): below the 10 % line, the hint is not a timing fact to carry.
reading (R2; pass 0 = DRAM, one warp, on.all-SM block cells: pass 1 of the grid = all cells is not an L2 measurement: 132 x W spoilers of 4 MiB push the table out of the L2 (pass 1 t_first 924-1133 against 360-386 on one SM). Pass 0: h100 W = 1 980 / 1510, W = 4 1413 / 1846; b300 1136 / 1648 and 1224 / 1685.

what the per-iteration values show (same.levels: the wait of a one-row load is not one number. b300: about 640 (56 % of the slots) or about 1010 (36 %); h100: about 600, 745 and 805. A slot keeps its level from launch to launch (b300 21 of 28 iterations identical in all four launches, h100 23 of 28; plain and hint cells agree on 99 / 106 of 112) and the 32 adjacent lines of the same slot take the level of the slot (b300 slot levels 640 -> 750, 1010 -> 1140 with 32 lines). So the DRAM-miss latency depends on where the data lives (unit at least 4 KiB), as the L2 far hit does, and a load on several rows waits for its slowest row: with two or more rows the far level is nearly always present.
what the per-iteration values show (same.occasional slow accesses: in launches 1-4 about 7 % (h100) / 5 % (b300) of one-row loads are 200-450 cycles above their slot's level, not tied to the slot. With L rows the share of iterations above the far level is 10 / 11 / 25 / 25 / 59 % for L = 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 on b300 (1 - 0.97^L gives 6 / 11 / 22 / 39 / 62 %).
what the per-iteration values show (same.first launch of the process: most slots cost 800-1100 cycles more the first time they are read in the process (launch 0; later iterations of launch 0 less often), never again: a first-touch cost of a unit much larger than a slot. Excluded from all medians above, not modelled; whether the cold reference of the suite contains it is not known.
what the per-iteration values show (same.engine: one DRAM latency for every miss (697.9 / 874.9, between the hardware levels), home side by line parity, far extra only on L2 hits; a miss on any number of rows costs the same. That is the 100-400 cycles the replay is short on every pass-0 cell with more than one row.

addenda.no rule yet: the judged cells of R2 cannot be scored before the unit of the levels and their dependence on the SM are known; nothing installed.

run_2.pair cells (unit of the level): k_pair: per iteration row A = the slot of run 1 (4-KiB slot by hash of the iteration), row B = A + delta inside the table; every lane reads the same 16 bytes; clock, load A, use, clock, load B, use, clock: the two waits are recorded separately. delta = 128 B, 4 KiB, 64 KiB, 2 MiB, 64 MiB; one warp, grid 1, 32 iterations, 5 launches, plain loads, pass 0 only.
run_2.matrix cells (SM against address): k_single_plain, L = 1, grid = all SMs, but only one CTA (argument active_cta) executes the pass, the others return at once; the slots are the same for every CTA (hash of the iteration only). active_cta = 0, 11, .., 121 (12 cells), 5 launches each; the output has the SM id (%smid) of the active CTA and every iteration's wait.
run_2.predictions: engine: every wait about 722 (h100) / 900 (b300), whatever the address and the SM. If the level belongs to a region of size R: A and B have the same level for delta < R and are independent beyond (same-level share p^2 + q^2 with the one-row shares). If the level is the SM's side against the region's home: for a fixed slot the SMs split into groups with different levels and every SM sees both levels; if it belongs to the address alone every SM sees the same level for a slot.
run_2.judging: R = the smallest delta at which the same-level share falls to the independent value (launches 1-4, iterations 4-31, levels cut at 700 / 780 on h100 and 800 on b300, slow accesses above 900 / 1200 set aside); the matrix is reported as slots x SMs with the level. A rule (latency of a DRAM miss by the region's level; a request waits for its slowest region) is then written with the levels of the one-row cells only and judged as R2 says (L = 32 far and adjacent, block W = 1, gather_latency one-warp cells, replay within 15 % on the block cells). The occasional slow accesses stay unmodelled unless run 2 ties them to something a trace knows.

run_3 (side map).cells: matrix cells of run 2 for EVERY CTA of an all-SM grid, in one process: sweep active_cta = 0 .. grid - 1, one launch per active CTA (L2 pushed out before each launch as before), same shared pages, L = 1, far, plain, 32 iterations; three sweeps, the first discarded (first touch in the process). Output per launch: SM id and the 32 waits.
run_3 (side map).derivation: per SM and page the median of sweeps 1-2 (pass 0); SMs are grouped by the sign pattern of (wait - the page's median over SMs); per SM: group, median wait on its fast pages and on its slow pages; cross table of group against gpc, placement_domain and l2_partition of sm_topology.json.
run_3 (side map).predictions: b300: two groups, split by gpc ({0, 1, 2, 4} against {3, 5, 6} and whatever the unsampled gpcs do), about 650 / 1040 for every SM. h100: not predicted; the installed l2_partition column is tested (run 2 says it fails).
run_3 (side map).judging: a device's side table is taken from this run if at least 95 % of its SMs fall into two groups with opposite page patterns and the group is a function of gpc (or the table is listed per SM if not of gpc); the near and far latencies are the medians over SMs. If a device shows more than two levels per SM (h100 in run 2), the table of levels is the result and the rule for that device is written only after it is understood. The rule to install is then: a DRAM miss costs the near latency, plus the far extra when the page's home differs from the SM's side; the home of a page is drawn per 4-KiB page (the trace has virtual addresses: the split is by page index parity, which reproduces 'same inside a page, about half of the pages on each side'); a request waits for its slowest sector as today. Judged as R2 of the protocol: L = 32 far and adjacent, block W = 1 (t_first, t_all), gather_latency one-warp cells, replay within 15 % on the block cells.

rule (to install, experimental).statement: a DRAM miss costs the near latency when the page's home is on the SM's side and the near latency plus a far extra otherwise. The SM's side is its gpc's side (h100 gpc 1-4, b300 gpc 2, 5, 6, 7 on side 1; SMs without a gpc on side 0, as the six b300 SMs measured). The home of a page is per 4-KiB page; the trace has virtual addresses, so the engine takes the parity of the page index (same inside a page, half of the pages on each side, neighbouring pages differ: run 2 found 63 % of 4-KiB neighbours on different levels on b300). A request waits for its slowest sector, as today. Applies to every DRAM miss of the load path (plain loads, async copies, TMA loads): one fetch path.
rule (to install, experimental).values: the probe's wait contains 24 cycles of issue / use / port that the h100 replay shows with the installed leaves (722 against the 697.9 leaf). near = fast level - 24: h100 583, b300 616 (the 24 is taken over from h100: the b300 kernel has two instructions fewer in the window and there is no b300 replay; assumption, stated in the source). far extra = slow - fast: h100 190, b300 395. dram.latency_cycles changes from 697.9 / 874.9 (a mixture of the two levels in a pointer chase) to the near value.
rule (to install, experimental).not modelled: the occasional slow accesses (5-7 % of single-row loads, +200-450; they are what lifts L = 16 and 32 far rows to 1039-1424) and the first-touch cost of the first launch of a process. The L2 far-hit side (memory.l2_partition, line parity and its own SM column) is left as it is: no L2-hit data in this probe says it is the same side.
